meta.description: Curriculum-aligned practice bank with coding, debugging, design, testing, workflow, interview scenarios and the existing LeetCode catalogue.
meta.note: All workbook v7 questions are included, plus the earlier curated and LeetCode catalogue entries.

questions.title: Trace Git staging
questions.prompt: Create a repo with three files. Change two files, stage only one, run status and diff commands, then explain exactly what each area contains.
questions.acceptanceCriteria: Show working tree, index and HEAD states before and after each command.
questions.hint: Use git status --short, git diff and git diff --cached.
questions.prerequisites: Git, GitHub and developer workflow
questions.how: Attempt independently first. Write down assumptions, test normal and edge cases, then explain your reasoning and trade-offs.

questions.title: Recover from a mistaken commit
questions.prompt: Make a commit with an incorrect message, then correct it safely. Repeat with an accidental file included and explain when amend, restore and reset are appropriate.
questions.acceptanceCriteria: Preserve intended changes; explain the difference between undoing local and shared history.
questions.hint: Inspect git status and git log before changing history.
questions.prerequisites: Git, GitHub and developer workflow
questions.how: Attempt independently first. Write down assumptions, test normal and edge cases, then explain your reasoning and trade-offs.

questions.title: Resolve a realistic merge conflict
questions.prompt: Create a feature branch and main branch that edit the same README section. Merge, resolve the conflict, run checks and finish with a clean history.
questions.acceptanceCriteria: Demonstrate conflict markers, chosen resolution, merge commit and clean status.
questions.hint: Use git diff and inspect both branch versions before editing.
questions.prerequisites: Git, GitHub and developer workflow
questions.how: Attempt independently first. Write down assumptions, test normal and edge cases, then explain your reasoning and trade-offs.

questions.title: Design a useful pull request
questions.prompt: Prepare a pull request for a small Java feature. Write a concise title, context, implementation summary, test evidence and reviewer checklist.
questions.acceptanceCriteria: A reviewer can understand the change and reproduce the checks without asking for missing context.
questions.hint: Think from the reviewer’s perspective.
questions.prerequisites: Git, GitHub and developer workflow
questions.how: Attempt independently first. Write down assumptions, test normal and edge cases, then explain your reasoning and trade-offs.

questions.title: Build a safe .gitignore
questions.prompt: Create a Java project .gitignore that excludes build output, IDE metadata, logs and local secrets while keeping source and wrapper files tracked.
questions.acceptanceCriteria: Verify ignored files with git status and git check-ignore; explain any exception.
questions.hint: Never commit credentials or machine-specific generated files.
questions.prerequisites: Git, GitHub and developer workflow
questions.how: Attempt independently first. Write down assumptions, test normal and edge cases, then explain your reasoning and trade-offs.

questions.title: Diagnose rejected push
questions.prompt: Your push is rejected because the remote contains commits you do not have. Diagnose the state and integrate remote changes without overwriting another contributor’s work.
questions.acceptanceCriteria: Show safe fetch/rebase or merge workflow and verify the resulting graph.
questions.hint: Fetch first; inspect remote history before integrating.
questions.prerequisites: Git, GitHub and developer workflow
questions.how: Attempt independently first. Write down assumptions, test normal and edge cases, then explain your reasoning and trade-offs.

questions.title: Write a repository README
questions.prompt: Document a small command-line project with purpose, prerequisites, setup, run instructions, examples, tests and contribution notes.
questions.acceptanceCriteria: A new developer can clone and run it using only the README.
questions.hint: Test every command in a clean directory.
questions.prerequisites: Git, GitHub and developer workflow
questions.how: Attempt independently first. Write down assumptions, test normal and edge cases, then explain your reasoning and trade-offs.

questions.title: Plan a branching strategy
questions.prompt: A two-person team ships weekly features and urgent fixes. Propose a lightweight branch, review, release and hotfix workflow.
questions.acceptanceCriteria: Explain branch lifetime, review gates, merge strategy and rollback approach.
questions.hint: Prefer a simple workflow the team will actually follow.
questions.prerequisites: Git, GitHub and developer workflow
questions.how: Attempt independently first. Write down assumptions, test normal and edge cases, then explain your reasoning and trade-offs.
